production.note: US model years. KBB: 'Ferrari 599 GTB Fiorano (2007-2012)', with 2007 to 2011 model-year pages linked. Evo titles the car 'Ferrari 599 GTB (2006 - 2012)' (build years; unveiled at the 2006 Geneva show per Drive). The 599 GTO and SA Aperta are separate models.

configuration.note: Ferrari specification as printed by Drive; Evo panel: 'Engine | V12, 5999cc'

displacementL.note: 5,999 cc. Ferrari specification as printed by Drive: 'Total displacement 366.08 cu in 5998.953 cc'; Evo panel: 'V12, 5999cc'

aspiration.note: Evo: 'a naturally aspirated V12 – a derivative of the engine at the heart of the Enzo'

fuel.note: Petrol V12; fuel type inferred from the description.

drivetrain.note: Front-mid-mounted V12 ('entirely behind the front axle') driving the rear wheels; rear-wheel drive inferred from the description.

transmission.note: Ferrari specification as printed by Drive: 'Gearbox (six gears + reverse) Manual or F1'. Evo: 'only 30 buyers opted for' the manual. The F1 paddle-shift gearbox is an automated manual.

powerHp.note: Ferrari's rating is metric: 620 CV x 0.98632 = 612 hp. Quote (Ferrari specification as printed by Drive): "Maximum power 456 kW** (620 CV) at 7600 rpm" (reproduced on a second request; the article body also writes '620 hp at 7,600 rpm'). Evo's panel prints 611bhp: "Power | 611bhp @ 7600rpm" (rounding). No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: Ferrari's own figure in pounds. Quote (Ferrari specification as printed by Drive): "Kerb weight 3722 lb* 1689.788 kg" (beside "Dry weight 3482 lb* 1580.828 kg"). The asterisk's footnote was not reproduced on the page, so it is not known whether the figures assume optional equipment or which gearbox they describe; probably the F1 car, which nearly all buyers chose. Evo's specification panel agrees: "Weight | 1690kg" (evo-599; 3,726 lb). Step 1 of the weight order. European specification; no US-specific figure found.

sources.title: Ferrari 599 GTB (2006 - 2012) review: a V12 Ferrari for less than a Porsche 911

discrepancies.reason: Rounding and unit conversion: both describe the same Ferrari kerb weight; the spec sheet's pound and kilogram figures do not convert exactly into each other.
discrepancies.resolution: Used Ferrari's published pound figure, 3,722 lb.

discrepancies.reason: Rounding of the conversion from Ferrari's metric rating (620 x 0.98632 = 611.5).
discrepancies.resolution: Used 612 hp, the guide's conversion rounded to the nearest whole number.
